content.title: About
content.content: Steamed salmon is a tender piece of fish cooked by steaming without added fats. This method preserves most nutrients while keeping the flavor mild and slightly sweet. Salmon is considered one of the healthiest seafoods thanks to its high omega‑3 fatty acids, protein, and vitamin content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salmon can migrate over 3,000 km from the ocean to freshwater rivers to spawn.
In the wild, salmon change skin color with the season and breeding stage.
Steaming retains up to 90 % of vitamin D, which is important for bones and immunity.
Salmon is one of the few fish that contain significant amounts of astaxanthin, giving the flesh its pink hue.
In Japan, steamed salmon is often served with soy sauce and fresh ginger.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Salmon provides a complete set of essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D helps maintain strong bones, a robust immune system, and mood regulation.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as a powerful antioxidant protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Steaming requires no added oil, keeping the dish light and heart‑friendly.

items.title: Risk of heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Some salmon may contain mercury or other toxins; choose reputable sources.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Spoilage if not stored properly
items.content: Fresh fillets deteriorate quickly; keep them at 0 °C or lower and use within 1–2 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve steamed salmon hot, often with lemon, fresh dill, or soy sauce. It can be added to salads, rice dishes, or used as a filling for sushi rolls. For extra flavor, lightly season with salt and pepper before steaming.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh salmon in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C and cook within 24–48 hours. Frozen salmon should be kept at –18 °C for up to 3 months; thaw it in the refrigerator before cooking.
